name: Aces Up
description: Aces Up is a one-deck patience game where you discard lower top cards of a suit when a higher top card of that same suit is present. The objective is to finish with only the four aces.

overview.description: Aces Up is a one-deck patience game where you discard lower top cards of a suit when a higher top card of that same suit is present. The objective is to finish with only the four aces.

history.origins: Aces Up appears in 20th-century patience collections and became widely known through digital solitaire suites.
timeline: Early 1900s: Printed in patience rule compilations under names such as Aces High.
1990s onward: Popularized in desktop and web solitaire programs.
history.cultural: Known for simple rules and a low practical win rate, making it a classic replayable solitaire.
history.evolution: Core rules remained stable; most variation comes from restrictions on which cards may fill empty piles.

setup.players: One player only. Aces Up is a patience (solitaire) game played by a single player using one deck and four tableau piles, with a space for discards.
setup.dealing: Deal four cards face up, one to each tableau pile. The rest of the deck is the stock.
setup.equipment: One shuffled deck and table space for four tableau piles.

rules.objective: The player wins by discarding all cards except the four aces. When the game ends, only the four aces should remain in the tableau; a maximum score of 48 discarded cards indicates a win, hence the name Aces Up.
rules.gameplay: 1. Compare the top cards of the four tableau piles. 2. If two or more top cards share a suit, discard any lower-ranked card(s) of that suit; ace is highest. 3. If a tableau pile is empty, move any top card from another pile into that space. 4. When no further discard or move is available (or chosen), deal one new card onto each pile from stock. 5. Continue until stock is empty and no legal move remains.
keyRules: Aces are high and therefore never discarded by same-suit comparison.
Any top card may fill an empty pile in standard Aces Up.
No redeal of stock in the standard game.

strategy.basic: Create and preserve empty tableau spaces, since they are your main control tool.
strategy.intermediate: Prefer moves that expose buried high cards, especially aces and kings.
strategy.advanced: Delay dealing from stock when tactical moves remain, because each new row can lock useful moves.
tips: When several same-suit discards are possible, keep the highest card exposed.
Use empty slots to extract trapped aces before final stock deals.

variations.name: Aces-Only Fill
variations.description: Only an ace may be moved into an empty tableau space.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: This variation only tightens which cards may fill empty piles; engine overrides are not modeled yet.

variations.name: Easy Aces Up
variations.description: Allows moving any exposed card (not only top cards) to an empty space.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: This easier variant loosens move constraints but does not yet have explicit engine overrides configured.

scoring.description: Score by discarded cards; 48 discarded (4 aces left) is a complete win.
scoring.winCondition: Exactly four cards remain and they are the four aces.

synthesis.shortDescription: Discard lower same-suit top cards and manage empty spaces until only four aces remain.

hero.title: ACES UP
hero.subtitle: Idiot's Delight
hero.tagline: Four piles, one deck, only aces survive.
